hunks.baseline: After a brief silence, the Heavenly Power Demon parted his lips.
hunks.sol: After a brief silence, the Heavenly Power Demon spoke.

hunks.baseline: “……A public-urination criminal? Do not address this old man by such a disgraceful name.”
hunks.sol: “……A public-urination criminal? Do not call this old man by such a disgraceful name.”

hunks.baseline: *Ah. I messed up.*
hunks.sol: *Ah. My mistake.*

hunks.baseline: It seemed the former fiend who had once made his name known throughout the world found that name rather unpleasant.
hunks.sol: It seemed the fiend who had once spread his infamy throughout the world found that title rather unpleasant.

hunks.baseline: After thinking for a moment, I offered him a more suitable term than public-urination criminal.
hunks.sol: After giving it some thought, I offered him a more appropriate alternative.

hunks.baseline: “Hmm. Or how about a bedwetter?”
hunks.sol: “Hmm. How about bedwetter?”

hunks.baseline: “If you don’t like that, then *Little Pee-er of the New Nation*.”
hunks.sol: “If you don’t like that, then *The New Nation’s Little Pisser*.”

hunks.baseline: “This old man did not piss himself!”
hunks.sol: “This old man did not wet himself!”

hunks.baseline: “Then *The One Who Peed*. *A Midsummer Night’s Pee*, featuring the Kunlun Sect.”
hunks.sol: “Then *He Who Peed*. *A Midsummer Night’s Pee*, featuring the Kunlun Sect.”

hunks.baseline: I clicked my tongue as I looked at the Heavenly Power Demon, who couldn’t even come up with a proper retort.
hunks.sol: I clicked my tongue at the Heavenly Power Demon, who couldn’t even come up with a response.

hunks.baseline: “I don’t know what got into you that made you suddenly start talking to me, and I don’t want to hear it or exchange words with you. So eat your food and shit as much as you like. Shit or piss, I don’t care. Do both at once, for all I care.”
hunks.sol: “I don’t know what got into you and made you start talking all of a sudden, but I don’t want to hear it, and I don’t want to talk to you. So eat your damn food and relieve yourself to your heart’s content. Shit, piss, or both at the same time. Whatever you want.”

hunks.baseline: I had finished handing out the food and was just about to leave the underground prison when I turned around with an irritated expression.
hunks.sol: I had finished handing out the food and was about to leave the underground prison when I turned around with an irritated scowl.

hunks.baseline: “If you have something to ask, am I obligated to answer?”
hunks.sol: “And if you have something to ask, am I obligated to answer?”

hunks.baseline: But the Heavenly Power Demon, seized by an inexplicable desperation, refused to back down. Wearing scraps of what might once have been called clothing, he opened his mouth with a gleam in his eyes.
hunks.sol: But the Heavenly Power Demon, seized by some inexplicable desperation, refused to back down. Clad in scraps of cloth that might once have been called clothing, he looked at me with gleaming eyes.

hunks.baseline: I had been momentarily confused because the two sides called it by different names.
hunks.sol: The different names used by the two sides had confused me for a moment.

hunks.baseline: To most Murim warriors, including me, it was *your* Demonic Cult. But from the Demonic Cult’s perspective, it could only be *our* Divine Cult.
hunks.sol: To most Murim warriors, myself included, it was *your* Demonic Cult. But to members of the Demonic Cult, it could only be *our* Divine Cult.

hunks.baseline: Especially for the Heavenly Power Demon standing before me. Wasn’t he a fiend whose notoriety had once been considerable even among the Demonic Cult’s members?
hunks.sol: And the Heavenly Power Demon before me had been notorious even among the Demonic Cult’s fiends.

hunks.baseline: “That’s not difficult.”
hunks.sol: “That’s easy enough.”

hunks.baseline: “……What did you say?”
hunks.sol: “……What?”

hunks.baseline: “How would I know what that Demonic Cult buried way off in the distance is doing? If some new inmate from the Demonic Cult ends up using the cell next to yours, you can ask him.”
hunks.sol: “How would I know what the Demonic Cult is doing, holed up all the way out there? If a new inmate from the Demonic Cult ends up in the cell next to yours, ask him.”

hunks.baseline: The Heavenly Power Demon looked at me as if he couldn’t understand me at all.
hunks.sol: The Heavenly Power Demon stared at me as if he couldn’t understand.

hunks.baseline: “You are the Fire King’s successor. Yet you claim to know nothing about the Divine Cult?”
hunks.sol: “Are you not the Fire King’s successor? Yet you claim to know nothing about the Divine Cult?”

hunks.baseline: “Although my dantian is ruined, these old ears still function.”
hunks.sol: “My dantian may be ruined, but these old ears still work.”

hunks.baseline: “You’re quite spry for a man old enough to have one foot in the grave. How much do you know?”
hunks.sol: “You’re awfully sharp for a man with one foot in the grave. How much do you know?”

hunks.baseline: “That the Fire King is here receiving treatment for his injuries.”
hunks.sol: “Only that the Fire King is here to have his injuries treated.”

hunks.baseline: He was a rather perceptive old man.
hunks.sol: He was a perceptive old man.

hunks.baseline: Cheongpung had mentioned Jeok Cheongang’s name several times, but never loudly enough for the other prisoners to hear. Even if the Heavenly Power Demon had heard him, it would have been difficult to infer the circumstances from their conversations.
hunks.sol: Cheongpung had mentioned Jeok Cheongang’s name several times, but never loudly enough for the other prisoners to hear. Even if the Heavenly Power Demon had overheard him, it would have been difficult to infer the circumstances from those conversations alone.

hunks.baseline: *He keeps his mouth shut but his ears open.*
hunks.sol: *He keeps his mouth shut and his ears open.*

hunks.baseline: He was different from the other prisoners, who tried to persuade anyone they could at the slightest opening.
hunks.sol: He was different from the other prisoners, who tried every possible trick to win me over the moment they saw an opening.

hunks.baseline: “But why are you so curious about news concerning the Demonic Cult? You’ve been captured for a long time already.”
hunks.sol: “But why are you so curious about news of the Demonic Cult? You’ve been imprisoned for ages.”

hunks.baseline: “It has been more than forty years.”
hunks.sol: “It has been nearly forty years now.”

hunks.baseline: “The Great Faction War had already ended around then. Don’t you have some idea of what happened?”
hunks.sol: “The Great Faction War was already over by then. Don’t you have a general idea of what happened?”

hunks.baseline: “Some idea?”
hunks.sol: “A general idea?”

hunks.baseline: The Heavenly Power Demon gave a bitter smile and continued.
hunks.sol: The Heavenly Power Demon smiled bitterly.

hunks.baseline: “This old man was once an Elder of the Great Heavenly Demon Divine Cult. It was I who, obeying the solemn command of the Cult Leader, subjugated Qinghai Province and opened the first front of the holy war.”
hunks.sol: “This old man was once an Elder of the Great Heavenly Demon Divine Cult. It was I who obeyed the august command of the Cult Leader, subjugated Qinghai, and fired the opening shot of the holy war.”

hunks.baseline: “Holy war my ass.”
hunks.sol: “Holy war, my ass.”

hunks.baseline: *He’s a bigger deal than I expected.*
hunks.sol: *He’s a bigger deal than I thought.*

hunks.baseline: From the bits and pieces I had heard, the Demonic Cult had something called the Ten Elders or the Seven Elders—great fiends who held tremendous power.
hunks.sol: From the bits and pieces I had picked up, the Demonic Cult had immensely powerful fiends known as the Ten Elders or the Seven Elders or something like that.

hunks.baseline: I had assumed he wasn’t an ordinary fiend after seeing him piss all over the Kunlun Sect’s signboard. But I had never imagined that the shabby old man waiting to die in an underground prison had once been an Elder of the Demonic Cult.
hunks.sol: I had assumed he wasn’t an ordinary fiend from the moment I heard he had pissed on the Kunlun Sect’s signboard. But I had never imagined that the shabby old man waiting to die in an underground prison had once been an Elder of the Demonic Cult.

hunks.baseline: “Of course not. That was ages ago. I heard the title Heavenly Power Demon for the first time today.”
hunks.sol: “Of course not. That was ages ago. Today was the first time I’d even heard the title Heavenly Power Demon.”

hunks.baseline: “……Heh. Has it truly been that long?”
hunks.sol: “……Heh. Has it truly been so long already?”

hunks.baseline: As I watched the Heavenly Power Demon let out a hollow, self-deprecating laugh, I leaned my back against the wall of the prison.
hunks.sol: As the Heavenly Power Demon let out a hollow, self-mocking laugh, I leaned against the prison wall.

hunks.baseline: “So what does a former Elder of the Demonic Cult from forty years ago want to ask me?”
hunks.sol: “So what does a former Demonic Cult Elder from forty years ago want to ask me?”

hunks.baseline: “Tell me everything you know about the Divine Cult. All the news you have heard recently, without leaving anything out.”
hunks.sol: “Tell me everything you know about the Divine Cult. Every piece of recent news, without adding or omitting anything.”

hunks.baseline: “I don’t know. Something about this feels unpleasant.”
hunks.sol: “I don’t know. Something about this feels off.”

hunks.baseline: “This old man has already passed his ninetieth year. Both body and spirit are exhausted. This is the final request of an old man who has already been given his day to die.”
hunks.sol: “This old man is past ninety, and both body and spirit are exhausted. This is the final request of an old man whose days are already numbered.”

hunks.baseline: “The request of a fiend who committed all kinds of atrocities, you mean.”
hunks.sol: “The request of a fiend who committed every atrocity imaginable, you mean.”
The Heavenly Power Demon continued in a clear voice.

hunks.baseline: “I will willingly accept punishment for the lives I have taken. But what, exactly, does it mean to be a demon? The Divine Cult and your people opposed each other for many years, each relying on its own beliefs, and we merely lost a battle in which we wagered our fate. That is all.”
hunks.sol: “I will gladly pay for the lives I have taken. But what, exactly, makes something demonic? The Divine Cult and your people opposed each other for many years, each standing by its own convictions. We merely lost the struggle in which we staked our fate. That is all.”

hunks.baseline: The Heavenly Power Demon continued in a clear voice, almost lamenting.
hunks.sol: His voice took on a note of lament.

hunks.baseline: “Do you claim that such a thing alone is enough to determine who was right and who was wrong? The world back then was like a keg of explosives that could go off at any moment. If your side had been the first to cross Gansu and Qinghai and reach the Divine Cult, you would have slaughtered our followers under the shabby pretexts of the greater good and rooting us out at the source.”
hunks.sol: “Can that alone determine who was right and who was wrong? The world back then was like a powder keg that could explode at any moment. Had your side crossed Gansu and Qinghai first and reached the Divine Cult, you would have slaughtered our followers beneath the paltry excuses of serving the greater good and rooting out evil at its source.”

hunks.baseline: I closed my mouth at the quiet voice.
hunks.sol: His quiet voice silenced me.

hunks.baseline: A pair of eyes, blazing more fiercely than ever, stared at me.
hunks.sol: A pair of eyes blazed more fiercely than ever as they stared into mine.

hunks.baseline: They did not belong to an old man whose martial arts had been completely crippled and who was waiting for the day he would die.
hunks.sol: They were not the eyes of an old man whose martial arts had been completely crippled, waiting for the day he would die.

hunks.baseline: They belonged to a general and Supreme Peak master who had once led an entire force and swept across the world.
hunks.sol: They belonged to a general and Supreme Peak master who had once led an army and swept across the world.

hunks.baseline: “This old man saw it and experienced it firsthand. I saw how cruel human beings could become in a war of killing and being killed. Neither the followers of the Divine Cult who shouted for a holy war nor the Sect Leaders of the Nine Sects and One Gang who called for the destruction of demons were exceptions. Even…”
hunks.sol: “This old man saw it with his own eyes and experienced it firsthand. I saw how cruel men could become in a war of killing and being killed. Neither the followers of the Divine Cult who cried out for holy war nor the Sect Leaders of the Nine Sects and One Gang who called for the extermination of demons were exceptions. Even…”

hunks.baseline: At that moment, the fire in his eyes faded, and only his bitter voice remained, scattering through the air like ash.
hunks.sol: At that moment, the fire in his eyes died away. Only his bitter voice remained, scattering through the air like ash.

hunks.baseline: “Even the Cult Leader of the Divine Cult was like that. He lost the beliefs he had started with and fell into corruption. Yes. Perhaps, as you orthodox faction warriors claim, the Divine Cult really was a Demonic Cult.”
hunks.sol: “Even the Cult Leader was no exception. He lost the convictions with which he had begun and fell into corruption. Yes. Perhaps, as you orthodox faction warriors claim, the Divine Cult truly had become a Demonic Cult.”

hunks.baseline: In a way, what he had just said overlapped with something I had realized recently.
hunks.sol: In a way, what he had just said aligned with something I had recently come to understand.

hunks.baseline: *There are good people and bad people everywhere.*
hunks.sol: *Good people and bad people exist everywhere.*

hunks.baseline: The Demonic Cult and the orthodox Murim had been at odds for ages, each holding a match and watching the other beside a powder keg that could explode at any moment.
hunks.sol: The Demonic Cult and the orthodox Murim had been at odds for ages, each holding a match as they watched the other across a powder keg ready to explode.

hunks.baseline: The Demonic Cult had been the one to light the fuse in the end. But what if the orthodox faction had lit it first?
hunks.sol: The Demonic Cult had ultimately been the one to light the fuse. But what if the orthodox faction had struck the first match?

hunks.baseline: Would the Roaring Fury Swordsman and the Taeeul Merciless Sword have left ordinary Demonic Cult civilians who knew nothing about martial arts alone?
hunks.sol: Would the Roaring Fury Swordsman and the Taeeul Merciless Sword have spared ordinary Demonic Cult civilians who knew nothing of martial arts?

hunks.baseline: For a moment, those two men and the Heavenly Power Demon overlapped in my mind.
hunks.sol: For a moment, those two men overlapped with the Heavenly Power Demon in my mind.

hunks.baseline: Who was white, and who was black? Was there something unknown hidden in the history that had already passed?
hunks.sol: Who was white, and who was black? Was there something buried in the history that had passed?

hunks.baseline: I bit my lip hard and pulled my back away from the cold wall.
hunks.sol: I bit my lip and pushed myself away from the cold wall.

hunks.baseline: “Telling me things like that won’t do you any good.”
hunks.sol: “There’s no point telling me any of that.”

terminology_alerts.message: preferred glossary term appears in BASE but not SOL for this hunk

hunks.baseline: “……I know. Nothing is more futile than talking about the past that has already passed.”
hunks.sol: “……I know. Nothing is more futile than speaking of a past already gone.”

hunks.baseline: “I’m not as well-versed in the Demonic Cult as you think. If a knowledgeable beggar had been here in my place, he might have been able to give you the news you want.”
hunks.sol: “And I’m not as knowledgeable about the Demonic Cult as you think. If that well-informed beggar were here instead, he might’ve been able to give you the news you want.”

hunks.baseline: “I don’t know. It doesn’t seem that way. From what I’ve heard, it has managed to maintain its existence somehow.”
hunks.sol: “I don’t know. Apparently not. From what I’ve heard, it has managed to survive somehow.”

hunks.baseline: It was only because the name Dark Heaven had been attracting so much attention lately, but the Demonic Cult was still the orthodox Murim’s eternal archenemy by default.
hunks.sol: Dark Heaven’s name had drawn so much attention lately that it was easy to forget, but the Demonic Cult remained the orthodox Murim’s eternal archenemy.

hunks.baseline: On top of that, with its connection to Dark Heaven now under suspicion, the Murim Alliance’s headquarters in Henan was probably busy investigating both the Demonic Cult and Dark Heaven.
hunks.sol: And with a possible connection between the Demonic Cult and Dark Heaven now under suspicion, the Murim Alliance headquarters in Henan was probably busy investigating both.

hunks.baseline: “I did hear that it shrank miserably after suffering an enormous blow during the Great Faction War.”
hunks.sol: “I did hear that the Demonic Cult suffered devastating losses in the Great Faction War and shrank to a shadow of its former self.”

hunks.baseline: The Central Plains was not called the center of the world for no reason.
hunks.sol: The Central Plains was not called the center of the world for nothing.

hunks.baseline: Unlike the orthodox Murim, which had recovered a considerable portion of its losses by absorbing the region’s abundant resources, goods, and population like a sponge, the Demonic Cult had been forced into the Tianshan Mountains while bearing the full weight of its tremendous losses.
hunks.sol: The orthodox Murim had absorbed the region’s abundant resources, goods, and population like a sponge, recovering much of what it had lost. The Demonic Cult, by contrast, had been forced to bear the full weight of its tremendous losses as it retreated into the Tianshan Mountains.

hunks.baseline: “……Of course. It was a war that mobilized the full strength of the Divine Cult.”
hunks.sol: “……Of course. It was a war in which the Divine Cult mobilized its full strength.”

hunks.baseline: He muttered quietly, a self-deprecating smile appearing at the corner of his mouth.
hunks.sol: He muttered under his breath, a self-mocking smile touching his lips.

hunks.baseline: “Heh. We once devoured half the world, and now we are utterly pathetic. I should have stopped the Cult Leader, even if it cost me my life, when he accepted vicious criminals like the Qilian Three Fiends and the Yin-Yang Twin Ghosts. Though, come to think of it, that was when the Cult Leader began to change as well.”
hunks.sol: “Heh. We once swallowed half the world, and now we are reduced to this pitiful state. I should have stopped the Cult Leader, even at the cost of my life, when he accepted vicious criminals like the Qilian Three Fiends and the Yin-Yang Twin Ghosts. Then again, that was when the Cult Leader himself began to change.”

hunks.baseline: “You may not know them, but there were men like that long ago…”
hunks.sol: “You may not know of them, but long ago, there were men called—”

hunks.baseline: “I don’t know much about the Qilian Three Fiends, but I know the Yin-Yang Twin Ghosts.”
hunks.sol: “I don’t know the Qilian Three Fiends, but I know the Yin-Yang Twin Ghosts.”

hunks.baseline: “How could someone who has never even heard this old man’s title know the Yin-Yang Twin Ghosts?”
hunks.sol: “How can someone who has never even heard this old man’s title know of the Yin-Yang Twin Ghosts?”

hunks.baseline: “Well, you see…”
hunks.sol: “Well…”

hunks.baseline: I scratched the back of my head and continued.
hunks.sol: I scratched the back of my head.

hunks.baseline: “I tend to remember the title of anyone I’ve fought. Especially when they’re masters of that caliber.”
hunks.sol: “I tend to remember the title of anyone I’ve fought. Especially masters of that caliber.”

hunks.baseline: “Technically, I only fought one of them—the Yang Ghost. Our Old Master—no, Master—killed the Yang Ghost. The Yin Ghost was killed by some crazy bastard and followed his friend to the afterlife. Anyway, do these fucking bastards think Henan is Gotham City…?”
hunks.sol: “Technically, I only fought one of them—the Yang Ghost. Our Old Master—no, my master—killed the Yang Ghost. The Yin Ghost was killed by some crazy bastard and followed his friend into the afterlife. Seriously, do these fucking bastards think Henan is Gotham City or something…?”

hunks.baseline: The Heavenly Power Demon froze with his mouth hanging open. Then he hurriedly poured out his words.
hunks.sol: The Heavenly Power Demon froze with his mouth hanging open, then hurriedly poured out his questions.

hunks.baseline: “T-the Yin-Yang Twin Ghosts! How did those men survive and emerge into the Murim? And in Henan, no less? Did the Divine Cult raid Shaolin?”
hunks.sol: “T-the Yin-Yang Twin Ghosts! How did those men survive and reappear in the Murim? And in Henan, no less? Did the Divine Cult launch a surprise attack on Shaolin?”

hunks.baseline: “They did make a hell of a mess at Shaolin. But it wasn’t the Demonic Cult’s doing.”
hunks.sol: “They did raise hell at Shaolin, but it wasn’t the Demonic Cult’s doing.”

hunks.baseline: “Th-then who did it? Whose doing was it?”
hunks.sol: “Th-then who was responsible? Who did it?”

hunks.baseline: I had expected as much, but the Heavenly Power Demon really knew nothing about how the current Murim worked.
hunks.sol: I had expected as much, but the Heavenly Power Demon truly knew nothing about the current state of the Murim.

hunks.baseline: The only outsider he had spoken with was Old Man Gung.
hunks.sol: The only outsider he ever spoke to was Old Man Gung.

hunks.baseline: *Well, it’s not like that old man is the type to kindly explain things.*
hunks.sol: *Not that the old man is the type to explain things out of kindness.*

hunks.baseline: Not unless he considered severing tendons a form of kindness.
hunks.sol: He might kindly sever someone’s tendons, though.

hunks.baseline: After thinking for a moment, I decided to tell him the truth.
hunks.sol: After a moment’s thought, I decided to tell him the truth.

hunks.baseline: The Heavenly Power Demon had no chance of leaving the underground prison before his death anyway.
hunks.sol: The Heavenly Power Demon would never leave the underground prison before he died anyway.

hunks.baseline: And now that Dark Heaven, once a top-secret matter, was gradually spreading through word of mouth among several major sects, there was no reason it would cause trouble.
hunks.sol: Besides, Dark Heaven’s existence had once been top secret, but word was already spreading among the major sects. Telling him would cause no harm.

hunks.baseline: “Um, I’m not sure how to put this.”
hunks.sol: “Uh, I’m not sure how to put this.”

hunks.baseline: “Wait a second.”
hunks.sol: “Hold on.”

hunks.baseline: At last, I found the right term. Admiring my own cleverness, I opened my mouth.
hunks.sol: At last, I found the perfect term. Impressed by my own brilliance, I opened my mouth.

hunks.baseline: “I’m not sure whether it was a job change or an internal departmental transfer, but until they died, they were working for someplace called Dark Heaven instead of the Demonic Cult…”
hunks.sol: “I don’t know whether they joined another company or merely transferred to a different department, but until they died, they were working for a group called Dark Heaven instead of the Demonic Cult…”

hunks.baseline: In the end, I couldn’t finish speaking.
hunks.sol: In the end, I couldn’t finish.

hunks.baseline: The sound of hurried footsteps approached, and a familiar face appeared.
hunks.sol: Hurried footsteps approached, and a familiar face appeared.

hunks.baseline: “What’s with all the ‘B’factors’? Are you looking for the police chief who lives in Namcheon-dong?”
hunks.sol: “Why do you keep going ‘b’factor, b’factor’? Are you looking for Chief Seo from Namcheon-dong?”

hunks.baseline: “Yeah, yeah. You probably hit the sauna, ate together, and did the whole nine yards.”
hunks.sol: “Yeah, yeah. I’m sure you went to the sauna, ate together, and did the whole nine yards.”

hunks.baseline: Cheongpung had stuffed both cheeks full of snacks, and he was still carrying an armful of food wrapped in paper.
hunks.sol: Cheongpung had stuffed both cheeks full of snacks, yet he still carried an armful of food wrapped in paper.

hunks.baseline: I pulled out a well-roasted duck leg and was about to bite into it when I held it out toward the person I had momentarily forgotten.
hunks.sol: I pulled out a nicely roasted duck leg and was about to sink my teeth into it when I remembered the man I had momentarily forgotten and held it out to him.

hunks.baseline: “Want some?”
hunks.sol: “Want one?”

hunks.baseline: And at last, I came face-to-face with the sight of the Heavenly Power Demon, frozen like a stone statue.
hunks.sol: Only then did I finally see the Heavenly Power Demon, frozen like a stone statue.
